### 2026-10-08: ## Starbie PCB and firmware

**3h**

## Starbie PCB and firmware

This session I designed my Starbie board in KiCad, following the Half Life guide and changing a few things to make it mine.

**What I did**
- Added the footprint and symbol libraries and drew the schematic: XIAO ESP32-C3, OLED, MPU6050 header, DHT11 and two buttons.
- Found that the guide forgot to mention a 10k pull-up resistor for the DHT11, so I added it.
- Fixed a mistake where most pins were on the same net, which would have shorted everything. The schematic now has no errors.
- Drew my own star-shaped board outline, placed the parts and routed every trace. DRC passed apart from a harmless courtyard error.
- Exported the Gerbers and uploaded everything to GitHub: https://github.com/den4ik9591/starbie-pcb

**Making it mine**
- Star-shaped PCB
- Replaced the PET menu item with DANCE
- Added a blinking sparkle effect behind the pet

**Problem I fixed:** Arduino gave a "redefinition" error because I had two `.ino` files in one folder. I kept just one.

**Next:** order the parts, build the board and test the firmware.

### 2026-10-11: ## Starbie: making my own pet image (1 hour)

**1h**

## Starbie: making my own pet image (1 hour)

This session I made my own pet image for Starbie and converted it so the OLED can display it.

**What I did**
- Drew a black and white image for my pet.
- Converted it to code with image2cpp

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 205216](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/eFI1qbxtPGZmzLCX4oomo3SgE8LA1rVP/70a84bf1992fbe8d6a3cd2a7c12fe34e535afdc6a1b8a48d1fe982317d987236.png)

, which turns the picture into a byte array the Arduino code can draw.
- [Pasted the byte array into `PET_SPRITE` in my sketch, and changed the width and height to match my image]

**What I learned**
- The OLED is 1-bit, so every pixel is either on or off. That's why the image has to be black and white.
- image2cpp turns each row of pixels into bytes, and the width has to be divisible by 8.

**Next:** test my sprite in a simulator and keep improving the project.
